conviction_note: This name's print is historically a small, positively skewed event - median 1.8%, five of seven up, and across seven prints the worst reaction was -3.98% while the only two moves above 4% were +8.96% and +13.23% - so the whole 47.7% de-rating from the high happened between prints; the corpus adds only a weak peer read-through and no negative company disclosure in August, which is worth about half the median, positive.

findings.finding: Dollar General, the closest value-retail comparable, beat one week before this print, and the OLLI capture contains no company disclosure in the whole of August 2026 - only two passive 13G/A filings on 2026-08-06 and 2026-08-13, with no 8-K since the 2026-06-15 annual-meeting filing - while the stock drifted 6.17% lower over twenty sessions to sit 47.7% below its 52-week high after a fall from about $140 to about $60 in six months.

findings.why_not_priced: The pre-print drift is the whole of the evidence the market has been acting on, and this name has no captured sell-side preview, no news document and no consensus figure other than an automated estimize relay of $1.14 whose stated report date, 08/27, is wrong. Against that, a peer beat landed a week earlier and the company itself has disclosed nothing negative. The reason I sign it positive rather than zero is the shape of the historical distribution: in seven prints the downside has never exceeded -3.98% while the upside has twice exceeded 8%, so the pre-print markdown has repeatedly not been validated by the print. I am keeping the number to half the median because this is genuinely weak: the finding rests on one retail message for the peer read-through, and the drawdown itself - a JP Morgan downgrade, Walmart cutting prices into the discount channel, 'the next Big Lots' - is a real bear case that the print will not settle.
findings.independence: From a different source in the same corpus: a 2026-08-24 message reports Fidelity increasing its OLLI holding by 29% in the prior quarter, and the filings index independently shows two SCHEDULE 13G/A filings inside one week (2026-08-06 and 2026-08-13), both consistent with institutions adding into the drawdown rather than leaving.

a quantified tariff-refund benefit: the corpus contains a single retail question of 2026-06-26 asking whether Ollie's will capitalise on 'the tariff refunds that retailers are receiving', and nothing that sizes it, so I did not build a finding on what could be a material one-time gross-margin item
any Form 4 activity at all in the 400-day index window near the print - no insider buying into a 47% drawdown, which is a mild negative
the content of the JP Morgan downgrade of 2026-07-08 - it reaches the corpus only as retail commentary
any news document: the OLLI capture is 80 EDGAR rows swept twice plus three StockTwits blobs, with no news bodies
a comp-sales or traffic datapoint for the July quarter, or any read on the Walmart price-cut threat's actual effect
baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-up, which is -3.04% over five days and -6.17% over twenty, and it leans on the reaction history, where five of seven were up and no reaction has been worse than -3.98%.
